candidates.source_title: Resident escapes from second floor as fire tears through sheltered housing flat
candidates.source_summary: A team of three fire engines attended the scene
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Fire crews rushed to a sheltered housing residence in Middleton this evening (November 5) after a blaze broke out at a second-storey flat. Eyewitness reported seeing fire engines and police parked on Sedgley Street and Nelson Street, responding to a fire that had broken out at Lonsdale Court. The building provides sheltered housing to the over-60s and is managed by Rochdale Borough Council. Three fire engines rushed to the scene where the building and neighbouring flats were evacuated. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter The fire service said that one resident 'self-rescued' from the property before they arrived and that safety checks were ongoing now that the fire was extinguished. A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said, “Just before 7pm this evening (Thursday, 5 th November), firefighters were called to reports of a fire at a supported living residence on Nelson Street in Middleton. “Three fire engines from Chadderton , Blackley and Heywood fire stations quickly arrived at the scene, where a flat on the second floor of the building was alight. "One casualty self-rescued before the arrival of the fire service and was assessed at the scene by colleagues from North West Ambulance Service (NWAS). Residents in the neighbouring flats were evacuated and are being supported by Rochdale Homes. “The fire has now been extinguished with some crews remaining at the scene while safety checks are carried out to the building.”

candidates.source_summary: Families are being warned to watch out for the symptoms of measles after confirmed cases in the borough.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Families are being warned to watch out for the symptoms of measles after confirmed cases in the borough. Measles can lead to serious health issues if it spreads to other parts of the body, or is contracted by someone who is vulnerable such as babies and people with weakened immune systems. Rochdale Council shared: “Positive cases of measles have been identified in the borough with some cases coming into A&E. “As a precaution please be aware of high fever, runny nose, cough, red and watery eyes, Koplik spots — small red spots with bluish-white centres inside the mouth — and a rash that starts on the face and behind the ears that spreads across the body. “Measles can cause serious complications and, in some cases, even be fatal. “If you or your children haven’t received an MMR vaccine, now is a good time to book one. Speak to your GP today to book one.” READ MORE: Planners can’t get over ‘out-of-character’ fence The MMRV vaccine helps protect children against measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox (varicella). It is usually given to children when they are 12 months and 18 months old. Some older children are also offered it.

Images from the scene showed three police vehicles close to the cordon and what appeared to be discarded clothing on a pavement. Officers from Greater Manchester Police could be seen making door-to-door inquiries in the aftermath of the incident. Witnesses were also spoken to at the scene. The closure of Limetrees Road led to significant congestion in Middleton town centre. Greater Manchester Police said a man in his 30s has been taken to hospital where he is being treated for serious injuries. No arrests have yet been made in relation to the incident and enquiries are ongoing, the force said. candidates.source_title: Preview: Fleetwood Town vs Rochdale - prediction, team news, lineups - Sports Mole
candidates.source_summary: Sports Mole previews Saturday's FA Cup clash between Fleetwood Town and Rochdale, including predictions, team news and possible lineups.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Aiming to record three consecutive successes at their Highbury Stadium fortress, Fleetwood Town host fellow League Two outfit Rochdale for a clash in the first round of the FA Cup on Saturday afternoon. The Cod Army have taken Arsenal's scalp on home soil in recent times in the EFL Cup, whilst the Dale are struggling to get a grip on the fourth tier following their promotion from the National League. Despite mulling around in the lower reaches of the League Two standings since their League One relegation in 2024, Fleetwood Town have enjoyed the spotlight recently after a historic cup success. On October 27, the Cod Army welcomed Premier League champions Arsenal to Highbury and knocked their visitors out of the EFL Cup, with the hosts earning a quarter-final tie with Everton in the middle of December. Scoring in both the beating of the Gunners and last weekend's 3-1 third-tier victory over Bristol Rovers, Aaron Loupalo-Bi is experiencing a breakthrough campaign in senior football, with the Fulham loanee netting five competitive goals for Fleetwood so far. That success over the Gasmen last time out extended the Cod Army's unbeaten run at Highbury Stadium to five matches (W4 D1) in all competitions, whilst Matt Lawlor 's men have lost just once across seven home league contests to date. Rather unsurprisingly, that sole Lancashire loss came at the hands of Saturday's visitors Rochdale in September, when first-half efforts from Dajaune Brown and Aden Flint sealed maximum League Two points for the Dale. Rochdale are back in the EFL this campaign following a three-year absence, winning the National League playoff final over Boreham Wood at Wembley Stadium, with that particular clash decided by penalty kicks.

candidates.source_title: Ring of Red motorcycle ride to support Heywood veterans on Remembrance Sunday
candidates.source_summary: More than 1,000 motorcyclists are expected to take part in the 13th annual Ring of Red M60 ride on Remembrance Sunday, 8 November.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: More than 1,000 motorcyclists are expected to take part in the 13th annual Ring of Red M60 ride on Remembrance Sunday, 8 November. The event will raise money for Heywood Veterans Association, which supports veterans in Heywood, Middleton and surrounding areas. Riders wearing red will travel around the M60 in a procession intended to resemble a giant poppy around Manchester when viewed from above. The non-competitive Ride of Respect honours members of the Armed Forces, past and present, and remembers those who died in service. Participants will gather from 8am at the westbound HGV parking area at Birch Services before departing at 1pm. The route will take riders onto the M62 before joining the M60 at junction 18 and continuing around the Manchester ring road. Organisers say the westbound HGV parking area will be closed to heavy goods vehicles from Saturday night until 2.30pm on Sunday. Heywood Veterans Association is the event’s nominated charity for 2026. Money raised through the sale of official red T-shirts, hoodies and patches will support its work.

candidates.source_title: Planners can’t get over ‘out-of-character’ fence - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Wooden fencing which replaced a low boundary wall has been described as "oppressive and enclosing" by planners.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Wooden fencing which replaced a low boundary wall has been described as “oppressive and enclosing” by planners. Lewis Mahoney applied to Rochdale Council for retrospective planning permission to remove the original boundary wall and raised beds to create a new garden wall and 1.8m high timber fencing at 1 Bates Close, Rochdale. But the changes to the corner plot have drawn criticism from the council’s planning department. A planning officer’s report said: “The application proposes the retention of a 1.8m high close-boarded fence which has been constructed adjacent to the public footpath at the boundary of the site without the benefit of planning permission. The original boundary wall at 1 Bates Close. Image: Google “The surrounding street scene is characterised by an absence of hard boundary treatment; most dwellings open directly to the public footpath, and in cases where there is boundary treatment, this is characterised by low-rise timber fencing or similar. “The proposed 1.8m high boundary fencing would therefore be at odds with this established character and would appear as an incongruous, out-of-character addition to the street scene which would be detrimental to the established character of the street scene. “The site location on the junction of Bates Close and hard against the public footpath would mean that the development would be readily visible from the public realm and surrounding dwellings and would read as an oppressive and intrusive form of development.

candidates.source_title: Enjoy spectacular free Ignite Fire Festival in Rochdale - Manchester Evening News
candidates.source_summary: The festival will run from Friday, November 20 to Sunday November 22, delivering magical trails of fire, lights and sound
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The festival will run from Friday, November 20 to Sunday November 22, delivering magical trails of fire, lights and sound The countdown to Christmas begins in Rochdale with the return of the spectacular Ignite Fire Festival. Providing magical, family-friendly entertainment, Ignite Fire Festival will once again transform the square and gardens around Rochdale Town Hall into a magical adventure featuring fire, lights and sound, with new pathways and parkland on Broadfield Slopes. This free-to-attend night-time event will run for three evenings, Friday, November 20 to Sunday, November 22, 2026, and be open from 5pm to 8pm. Organiser Rochdale Development Agency is promising new dazzling trails and attractions to make it the best yet. Taking centre stage is the Body, which takes visitors on a journey through six zones of the human body using fire, light, sound and special effects. The multi-sensory experience is Walk the Plank's most ambitious fire-and-light installation, from multi-award-winning outdoor arts specialists. Having previously travelled across the globe, from Ireland to Canada Ignite Fire Festival will see its north-west premiere. Audiences can expect to be mesmerised on this dramatic, spellbinding journey as they walk through the glowing embers of human metabolism - the silent furnace that keeps us alive, continuously generating heat to power all the body's functions. Using cutting-edge technology, the experience will entertain and educate, providing a deeper understanding of what lies beneath. Bev Ayre, senior producer at Walk the Plank, said: "The countdown is on until we bring Body to Ignite and we can't wait. We hope our dynamic fire and light installation will not only entertain audiences but also inspire everyone to learn more about what makes us all human. We’re also excited to illuminate the slopes and gardens with fire and special effects, framing the beautiful town hall."

Gymbound will become the club’s official club-wide main shirt sponsor, with its branding set to feature on the front of playing shirts across every section of the club, from its youngest players through to its senior teams as Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its historic 70th anniversary in 2028. The agreement will also see Gymbound, in Eagle Technology Park, Queensway, support Rochdale Mayfield’s open-age pre-season training programme, providing players with access to a modern fitness environment to help improve strength, conditioning, fitness and overall preparation ahead of the new season. The partnership will introduce exclusive membership opportunities for Rochdale Mayfield players and club members, encouraging greater participation in physical activity and making fitness more accessible. Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC founder Carl Abraham said: “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Gymbound on board as our club-wide main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. “This is a significant partnership for Rochdale Mayfield and another major step forward in our ambition to become the best amateur sports club in the borough. “As a club, we are constantly looking to build relationships with local businesses that share our values, ambitions and commitment to the community. Gymbound is a fantastic example of that. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our open-age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club.

candidates.source_summary: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. The court record states that Penrose threatened a police officer with a kitchen knife in a public place in a way that would cause a reasonable person to believe there was an immediate risk of physical harm. He was also convicted of possessing the kitchen knife without good reason or lawful authority in a public place. Penrose further threatened a second police officer with the knife in a public place before threatening the same officer with the weapon at a private address on West Starkey Street. He indicated guilty pleas to all four offences on April 27 and was convicted on the same date. The case was dealt with at Manchester Crown Court on Friday, October 30. The court imposed a hospital order, under which Penrose will be admitted to or detained at Prestwich Hospital.

candidates.source_body_excerpt: An Asda worker has been praised for her kindness after going above and beyond to support a recently widowed customer. Saheda Bibi, 43, has worked at Asda in Rochdale since 2012. After learning that a customer had lost her husband, Saheda promised the woman's daughter that she would look after her mum. The daughter, who lives in London, was worried about how her mum would cope on her own. Saheda reassured her by explaining which days she worked, allowing the customer to plan her shopping trips around her shifts. Since then, Saheda has helped the woman with her shopping, scanning and packing her items, making sure she has a chair to sit on and finding time for a friendly chat. Reflecting on the weekend, Byrne told club media: “It was a game that was important that we looked back over and looked through and it's a game we have to quickly learn from. “So our benefit now is we’ve got a game coming quickly, so we’re looking forward to that and to be able to go and put a performance on, it’s a game we need to win, it’s a cup competition and we want to progress to the next round, so that’s where the focus is.” Byrne continued: “I think when you come off a poor defeat and a poor performance couple with it, you definitely want an opportunity to go and rectify it and put it right, so when you have a game within a couple of days, that gives you the opportunity to go and do that and that’s exactly what we’ll be aiming to do.” Rovers reached the semi-final of this competition and only narrowly missed out on a first visit to Wembley since 2008 after losing to Stockport County in the semi-final. The South Yorkshire side have only ever won this competition once. That came in 2007 when Sean O’Driscoll’s men were triumphant over Bristol Rovers at the Millenium Stadium. “We want to go as far as we can,” said Byrne. “We made no bones about it last season and this season we have had some really good teams in our group, we’re down to the last game and it’s in our hands to progress to the next round.” The EFL Trophy is often seen as a competition for youngsters and squad players to get an opportunity. Byrne hinted that they’ll be some changes but also emphasized the importance of picking up a good result. He said: “It’s a game we want to win and the selection we have in mind is for that, to win the game and progress. “But there may be an opportunity for some players to get more minutes than they have in recent weeks but I think that's the nature of how the schedule is. It’s very hard to ask the same 11 to go time and time again. They’ll be opportunities in some areas but in others there won’t be.”

candidates.source_title: Appeal over student accommodation at former care home is dismissed - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: Planners' refusal of a bid to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been upheld.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: An appeal over plans to turn a former care home into university accommodation has been dismissed. The Al Sadiq Academy appealed to the Planning Inspectorate after Rochdale Council refused permission to change the use of the former Briarmede care home, in Rochdale Road, Middleton, into university accommodation. The plans included creating 11 en-suite bedrooms, with kitchens and dining hall/games room, library, study rooms, computer rooms and toilets on the ground floor. Planning offices recommended approval for the application, which would have included conditions the building is solely for the use of residents and was not used to provide classes, education services or private or community events at any time. But the application was called in by the council’s planning committee which refused it following concerns about the need for the facility, and the impact it would have on neighbours. In delivering the appeal decision, planning inspector K Mee said: “The main issues are whether the appeal site is a suitable location having regard to the local development plan, insofar as it relates to the type of accommodation; and the effect of the proposed development on the character of the surrounding area and the living conditions of neighbouring residents, with regard to noise and disturbance. “The appellant identifies a number of higher education institutions across Greater Manchester, including Hopwood Hall College opposite the appeal site, as potential sources of demand for student accommodation. “However, no substantive evidence has been provided to demonstrate that these institutions have been consulted regarding the proposals, nor that there is an identified unmet need for additional student accommodation either locally or across the wider area.

candidates.source_title: Decision made over rebuilding of Storage World - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_summary: The green light has been given for Storage World to be rebuilt in Middleton town centre.
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The green light has been given for Storage World to be rebuilt in Middleton town centre. Rochdale Council has approved Self-Storage Performance Management International Ltd’s planning application to replace the building in Old Hall Street after it was destroyed by fire in June last year. Instead of a like-for-like replacement, SSPMI will now create a £12 million smaller, taller, mixed-use building with self-storage units on the upper floors and commercial units on the ground floor. The new building will occupy half the footprint of the former Storage World units, but will include two extra storeys to deliver the same capacity inside. In documents submitted with the application, P4 Planning said: “The applicant’s key objective following the catastrophic fire is to replace the building with a suitable modern design that will bring back SME business activity and self-storage space as quickly as possible. “Through close engagement with the council planning and other departments, the applicant is keen to deliver a far better development, with a more appropriate design and format that will also bring wider regeneration benefits. “The mix of uses and economic benefits, design and wider potential benefits will all have a positive impact on the future regeneration of Middleton town centre. “The scale, mass and materials draw reference from the historic research and the site’s past, when Albany Mill was present on the site until 1975.”
